summary: This is a Snowflake SQL documentation page for the STRTOK_TO_ARRAY function, which tokenizes a string using a set of delimiters and returns the tokens as an ARRAY. It covers syntax, arguments (a required string and an optional delimiter set defaulting to a single space), NULL and empty-array behavior, and two examples splitting on '.' and on multiple delimiters '.@'. The page is listed under the Conversion/Casting category.
one_line: Snowflake SQL function STRTOK_TO_ARRAY splits a string on a set of delimiters and returns the tokens as an array.
key_facts: STRTOK_TO_ARRAY tokenizes the given string using the given set of delimiters and returns the tokens as an array.
The required argument is string, the text to be tokenized.
The optional delimiter argument is a set of delimiters, with a default value of a single space character.
The data type of the returned value is ARRAY.
If either parameter is NULL, STRTOK_TO_ARRAY returns NULL.
An empty array is returned if tokenization produces no tokens.
Example: SELECT STRTOK_TO_ARRAY('a.b.c', '.') returns the array ["a", "b", "c"].
Example: SELECT STRTOK_TO_ARRAY('user@snowflake.com', '.@') returns the array ["user", "snowflake", "com"].
The second example tokenizes on multiple delimiters, '.' and '@'.
The page is listed under the Conversion/Casting category of the function reference.
